newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Stet, RAI sign pay TV j-venture.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Stet, RAI sign pay TV j-venture.

text.p: Italian telecommunications holding Stet and state broadcaster RAI said on Wednesday they had signed a deal setting up a joint company to offer theme channels for pay television.
RAI said in a statement that as part of the deal, it would also take a 15 percent stake in Stet's multimedia unit Stream.

RAI will initially hold 80 percent of the new joint venture company with the remainder held by Stet, which is due to merge with its main operating unit Telecom Italia on Friday ahead of a privatisation later this year.
The Stet-Telecom group, which will be called Telecom Italia after its merger, will be able to exercise an option for a further 10 percent stake, the statement said.
"The accord also envisages the possibility of other partners entering the joint venture," RAI said. It gave no details of who those partners could be and gave no financial details.
RAI's stake in Stream could also rise to 30 percent, it said.
The joint-venture company intends to put together a package of theme channels, based on programmes from RAI and other providers, for Stream and other broadcasters.
The deal would consolidate Stream's position as a service provider, it said.

RAI said it and Stet/Telecom Italia planned to develop the accord within the framework of an overall digital television project based on a single platform open to other national and foreign operators.
RAI and Stet said in April they were planning a strategic alliance to develop a common digital standard for satellite and cable communications in Italy.

They said at the time that they wanted to develop a digital platform open to all multimedia services but if that proved impossible they aimed to create an autonomous digital platform which would act as a national "common carrier."

"This accord between RAI and Stet/Telecom Italia is a fundamental step towards the take-off in Italy of digital television based on an open and one of the most advanced platforms in the world," Stet managing director Tomaso Tommasi di Vignano said in the statement.
RAI chairman Enzo Siciliano said the deal "brings Italy closer to the rest of Europe and the world."
"Finally the serious foundations have been laid for the development of digital television and therefore a greater offer of audiovisual services," he added.
